Potato___Early_blight.symptoms: Dark brown to black necrotic spots with characteristic concentric rings creating a 'target board' effect on older leaves, yellow halo around lesions.
Potato___Early_blight.causes: High humidity (>85%), warm temperatures (24-29°C), alternating wet and dry periods, stressed plants with low nitrogen.
organic_control: Foliar spray of organic Copper oxychloride (3g/L) or Bordeaux mixture (1%).
Biological control using Trichoderma viride or Bacillus subtilis bio-fungicide.
Spray 5% Neem seed kernel extract (NSKE) at early onset.
chemical_control: Azoxystrobin 23% SC @ 1 ml/liter of water for systemic suppression.
prevention: Practice 3-year crop rotation with non-solanaceous crops.
Maintain adequate plant spacing to facilitate air circulation.
Use drip irrigation to prevent water splashing on leaves.
Destroy and burn crop residues after harvest.

Potato___Late_blight.symptoms: Water-soaked irregular dark green/brown lesions starting from leaf tips and margins; white fuzzy fungal growth on the underside during humid weather.
Potato___Late_blight.causes: Cool, wet conditions (15-20°C with >90% RH), continuous cloud cover, dew duration > 8 hours.
organic_control: Preventive spray of Copper hydroxide or Bordeaux mixture (1%) before rain.
Apply bio-agent Pseudomonas fluorescens @ 5g/L.
prevention: Use certified disease-free seed tubers (e.g. Kufri Jyoti / Kufri Girdhari).
De-haulm (cut foliage) 10-12 days before tuber harvest.
Avoid sprinkler irrigation in the late evening.

Potato___healthy.symptoms: Leaves exhibit uniform deep green coloration, firm turgid foliage, devoid of chlorosis, necrosis, or pest bites.
Potato___healthy.causes: Balanced soil nutrition, optimal irrigation, well-aerated sandy-loam soil.
organic_control: Continue standard organic fertility practices (Vermicompost 5 tons/ha).
Periodic foliar spray of seaweed extract (2 ml/L) for micronutrient support.
chemical_control: No chemical application required. Avoid prophylactic chemical overuse.
prevention: Regular scouting every 48 hours for early signs of aphids or blight.
Maintain soil moisture at 65-75% field capacity.

Tomato___Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Small, water-soaked circular to angular dark brown spots (1-3mm), often with greasy appearance and narrow chlorotic halo.
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.causes: Warm temperatures (25-30°C), driving rains, sprinkler irrigation causing overhead splash.
organic_control: Spray Copper-based bactericide mixed with Bacillus amyloliquefaciens.
Apply 0.5% copper sulfate with lime solution.
chemical_control: Streptocycline (Streptomycin sulphate + Tetracycline) @ 0.5 g/10L water combined with Copper Oxychloride (2.5 g/L).
prevention: Hot water treatment of seeds (50°C for 25 minutes) before sowing.
Disinfect pruning shears and staking tools regularly.
Do not cultivate or touch plants when foliage is wet.

Tomato___Early_blight.symptoms: Concentric rings on brown lesions resembling bullseye targets, typically beginning on lower older foliage.
Tomato___Early_blight.causes: High humidity, prolonged leaf wetness, low nitrogen stress.
organic_control: Spray cow dung slurry supernatant (10%) + Neem oil (3%).
Apply Trichoderma harzianum soil inoculation.
prevention: Stake and mulch tomato plants to prevent soil-to-leaf splashing.
Prune bottom 30cm of foliage as the plant matures.

Tomato___Late_blight.symptoms: Pale green turning dark olive-brown greasy lesions; white mildew growth under humid conditions; rapid stem girdling.
Tomato___Late_blight.causes: Cool, damp weather with high fog or rainfall, temperature between 16-22°C.
organic_control: Copper hydroxide 53.8% DF spray.
Propolis extract spray.
prevention: Plant resistant hybrid cultivars.
Avoid planting tomatoes adjacent to infected potato fields.

Tomato___Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.symptoms: Severe upward curling and cupping of leaflets, marked yellowing (chlorosis) of leaf margins, bushy stunted growth.
Tomato___Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.causes: High population pressure of whitefly vector during hot dry spells.
organic_control: Install yellow sticky traps @ 20-25 traps per acre.
Spray 5% NSKE (Neem Seed Kernel Extract) or 2% horticultural mineral oil.
Erect 40-mesh insect-proof netting in nursery.
chemical_control: Imidacloprid 17.8% SL @ 0.5 ml/L to control whitefly vector.
Diafenthiuron 50% WP @ 1 g/L for vector knockdown.
prevention: Grow border crops of maize, sorghum, or pearl millet (3 rows) as physical windbreak against vector.
Rogue out and bury infected virus-carrying plants immediately.

Tomato___healthy.symptoms: Leaves are vibrant emerald green, serrated edges intact, vigorous apical shoots, active flowering/fruiting.
Tomato___healthy.causes: Optimal fertigation, regulated pest scouting, balanced microclimate.
organic_control: Apply Panchagavya 3% or Jeevamrutha spray every 15 days.
Maintain mycorrhizal root associations.
prevention: Continue monitoring for sap-sucking pests.
Ensure proper trellising and support.

Corn___Common_rust.symptoms: Golden-brown to cinnamon-brown powdery pustules erupting on both upper and lower leaf surfaces.
Corn___Common_rust.causes: Cool, humid weather (16-25°C) with nearly 100% relative humidity.
organic_control: Wettable sulfur (80% WP) @ 3 g/L.
Spray Ampelomyces quisqualis hyperparasite.
prevention: Plant rust-tolerant hybrid corn varieties.
Sow early in the season to escape late fungal spore peaks.

Corn___Northern_Leaf_Blight.symptoms: Long, elliptical grayish-green or tan cigar-shaped lesions (2.5 to 15 cm long) parallel to leaf veins.
Corn___Northern_Leaf_Blight.causes: Moderate temperatures (18-27°C) with heavy dews and high humidity.
organic_control: Bio-fungicide Bacillus subtilis foliar spray.
Trichoderma viride field spray.
prevention: Deep plowing of maize stubbles to bury overwintering conidia.
Crop rotation with legumes or oilseeds.

Corn___healthy.symptoms: Broad, vibrant green leaves with prominent midrib, erect architecture, no lesions or chlorosis.
Corn___healthy.causes: Adequate nitrogen top-dressing, timely weeding, sufficient moisture at tasseling stage.
organic_control: Apply enriched compost and Azotobacter biofertilizer.
prevention: Inspect whorls for fall armyworm (FAW) egg masses.

Apple___Apple_scab.symptoms: Olive-green, velvety spots on upper leaf surfaces that turn brownish-black and corky; leaf distortion and early drop.
Apple___Apple_scab.causes: Cool, wet spring weather (10-20°C) with prolonged leaf wetness (6-12 hours).
organic_control: Lime sulfur spray during dormancy and pink bud stage.
Copper hydroxide spray at silver tip stage.
prevention: Rake and destroy fallen leaves in autumn or spray 5% urea to hasten decomposition.
Prune orchard canopies to maximize sunlight penetration and wind drying.

Apple___Black_rot.symptoms: Small purple flecks on leaves enlarging to circular lesions with tan centers and purple margins ('frogeye' pattern).
Apple___Black_rot.causes: Warm temperatures (24-27°C) combined with high rainfall or fire blight damage.
organic_control: Copper oxychloride spray.
Removal of dead mummified fruits and cankers.
prevention: Prune out dead wood, fire blight strikes, and cankers 15cm below visible damage.
Keep trees free from mechanical wounds.

Apple___healthy.symptoms: Dark green leaves with serrated margins, robust petiole attachment, glossy cuticle.
Apple___healthy.causes: Good orchard canopy management, balanced N-P-K-B-Ca nutrition.
organic_control: Foliar spray of micronutrient mixture with Boron and Zinc.
prevention: Maintain pheromone traps for codling moth and monitor mite populations.
